title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-23
korean_summary: 월요일 핵심: 휴일 전 회계장 CM 3개 답 확인, 영업부 비용 품의 상신. 트럭 계약 서류·항공료·응급처치 답 받기, 인사·안전 담당 회신.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Monday, November twenty-third. A new week starts today, but it is a short week. Tomorrow, Tuesday, is Vietnam Culture Day, a paid holiday. So today you have only one day before the break. Let's use it well.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

First, some good news from Saturday. You sent the weekly cash report to head office. You chose a supplier for the December electrical inspection, and you asked the compliance officer to make the purchase request. My director also sent some files to head office for the welfare plan. And you sent your answer on one worker's contract to head office. Well done.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The chief accountant's three answers on the CM plan.

What is it? This is about the chief accountant. On Saturday, you revised the tax CM for November and December. CM means cutting and making, our sewing fee. She sent back the updated estimated income statement. But she did not answer your three questions. You asked her again, and the deadline is today.

The three questions are simple. First, on Thursday she said the margin was too high, so CM must go down. On Friday she said she raised CM to increase revenue. These two reasons do not match. Which lines did she cut instead? Second, why did she raise CM on some lines without your approval? Third, she also said some November styles were already exported. So can those lines still change?

Why does it matter? The CM plan decides our invoices and our profit. If the reasons keep changing, you cannot report the plan to my director with confidence. Also, the December plan is due on the twenty-fifth.
Your first action today: Open her reply before ten o'clock. Check each answer against the file. If the answers do not add up, call her and go through the lines together.
Number two. The trucking documents from the import and export manager.

What is it? This is about the import and export manager. On Saturday morning, you sent her two reminders. One was for the Incoterms by buyer and ship mode, and the quotation sheet from each trucking company. That was due on Saturday, and it is now late. The other was about the trucking contracts. You asked three points. Has the first company signed yet? Can you see the revised appendix draft before it goes out? And what about the missing insurance certificates?

Why does it matter? We want each trucking company to take clear responsibility if cargo is lost or damaged. Without the insurance certificates and the appendix, we have no protection. And Wednesday has a fabric delivery.
Your first action today: Check her reply first thing. If nothing came, talk to her face to face before lunch. Agree on one firm date for everything.
Number three. The sales cost approval document.

What is it? This is the monthly cost we charge to the head office sales team. You closed the numbers on Saturday. Today, you need to put the approval document into the groupware. Your calendar has this for today.
Why does it matter? Tomorrow is a holiday. If you miss today, the document waits until Wednesday. Head office may also ask why it is late.

Your first action today: Open last month's document and use it again. Change the title, the amount, and the picture. Attach this month's cost file. Then send it for approval before the end of the day.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, from the HR contract staff. On Saturday, she answered your questions about one worker's contract. She also explained the leave days and the benefits. Check that her numbers match the summary you sent to head office. If something is unclear, you can say: "Could you show me how you got this number, step by step?"

Second, from the purchasing staff. You asked her for two flight fares by today. One is for a foreign manager going home on November twenty-ninth. He wants extra checked baggage. He gets his passport back on November twenty-fifth, so the date may need to move. The other is for another manager's Tet holiday trip in February. You can say: "Could you let me know where the fare check stands? I need it today because tomorrow is a holiday."

Third, from the compliance staff. On Saturday, you asked her five questions about the first aid training. Why was it not arranged before the certificates expired? How often must we renew it, and what is the legal basis? How will we track the dates? What is the minimum number of first aid staff by law? And can we take fewer people from the sewing lines? You can say: "Apart from these answers, is there anything else we need to prepare before December fifth?"

Fourth, from the compliance officer. You asked her to make the purchase request for the inspection this week. The quotation is valid until December ninth. You can say: "Please send me the purchase request by Wednesday, so that we can finish approval before the quote expires."

Fifth, from the accounting staff. She still owes the reasons for some accounts in the management versus tax profit file. You can say: "It has been three days since I asked, and I still don't have the reasons. Could you send them today?"
Part four. Replies I owe.

Reply one. The HR manager. She reviewed your 2027 salary evaluation plan. She agrees with doing the evaluation in December, one month earlier than last year. She also raised one risk. From January first, labor contracts must have an ID number and be uploaded to the labor department system. But the e-contract provider is not ready yet. If it is not ready in time, she will use paper contracts. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for the review. I agree with the December schedule. For the e-contract, please check with the provider again on December first, and let's decide paper or electronic by December tenth."

Reply two. The compliance officer, about firefighting system maintenance. She got quotations from several suppliers under the same conditions. She also asked other factories in our group. All of them have a maintenance contract with a supplier. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for checking with the other factories. Please itemize each quote by equipment, so that we can compare them line by line."

Reply three. The compliance officer, about the chemical test for the fusing machine. She sent before and after photos for a cleaning chemical. She says it works well. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for the test. Before we buy more, please tell me the price and how often we need to use it."

Reply four. A head office manager, about some import records. He expects the status today. Check with the import and export manager what she has found. Your first sentence could be: "Here is the status of the records. We checked each shipment, and here is what we found."
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Monday: The weekly firewood report to head office. The sales cost approval document. The chief accountant's three answers. The flight fares. The HR contract numbers. And the import records status for head office.
Tuesday, November twenty-fourth: Vietnam Culture Day. It is a paid holiday. Our collective labor agreement also expires that day. Today, ask the HR manager if the renewal is registered.

Wednesday, November twenty-fifth: A fabric delivery arrives at eight in the morning. Outside workers will unload it. A foreign manager gets his passport back. And the chief accountant should send the December CM plan.
Thursday, November twenty-sixth: The next week overtime report.
Part six. English review.
Let's review nine expressions from last week and the week before. Many of them will help you today, especially with the accountant and the suppliers.

The expression is "rationale." It means the reason behind a decision. For example, "Please explain the rationale for the CM change for each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please explain the rationale for the CM change for each style.
... ... ...

The expression is "rectify." It means to fix something that is wrong. For example, "The contractor must rectify the wrong part before we pay." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The contractor must rectify the wrong part before we pay.
... ... ...

The expression is "itemize." It means to list each cost on its own line. For example, "Please ask the suppliers to itemize the parts and installation costs." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please ask the suppliers to itemize the parts and installation costs.
... ... ...

The expression is "From now on, let's make it a rule that ..." You use it to set a new rule. For example, "From now on, let's make it a rule that every plan change needs my approval first." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. From now on, let's make it a rule that every plan change needs my approval first.
... ... ...

The expression is "Apart from ..., is there anything else ...?" It means you want to know about other things too. For example, "Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our tax code?" Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our tax code?
... ... ...

The expression is "Under ..., the company is required to ..." It means the law says we must do something. For example, "Under the safety law, the company is required to train first aid staff." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Under the safety law, the company is required to train first aid staff.
... ... ...

The expression is "Unless I hear otherwise by ..., I will ..." It means you will act if nobody says no. For example, "Unless I hear otherwise by three o'clock, I will submit the approval document." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by three o'clock, I will submit the approval document.
... ... ...

The expression is "My understanding is that ... Please correct me if I'm wrong." You use it to check a fact politely. For example, "My understanding is that the quote is valid until December ninth. Please correct me if I'm wrong." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. My understanding is that the quote is valid until December ninth. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...

The expression is "allocate." It means to share something out to each part. For example, "Please show me how you allocated the quantity to each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please show me how you allocated the quantity to each style.
... ... ...
Part seven. Role-play.
Here is the situation. It is Monday morning. The chief accountant comes to your desk with her answers on the CM plan. Listen to the conversation.
Accountant: Good morning, Mr Lee. I sent my answers to your three questions.
Anthony: Thank you. I read them. But I still don't understand one thing. On Thursday you said the margin was too high. On Friday you said you raised CM to increase revenue. What is the rationale?
Accountant: The quantity went up for November. So I had to move some lines.
Anthony: I see. Which lines did you cut more to balance it? The amounts should add up to the total change.
Accountant: I will show you the line list.
Anthony: Thank you. Also, some styles were already exported. Can those lines still change?
Accountant: No. Those invoices are already issued.
Anthony: Then please take them out of the plan. From now on, let's make it a rule that any plan change needs my approval first.
Accountant: Yes, Mr Lee. I understand. May I ask one thing? If the export quantity changes again in December, what should I do?
Anthony: Good question. Send me the new quantity and the CM for each style first. Then we decide together. Please do not change the plan on your own.
Accountant: Understood. I will send it to you before I update the file.
Anthony: Good. Please send me the final file by Wednesday. Unless I hear otherwise by then, I will report the current version to my director.
Now let's practice two key sentences.

First sentence. From now on, let's make it a rule that any plan change needs my approval first.
... ... ...
One more time. From now on, let's make it a rule that any plan change needs my approval first.
... ... ...

Second sentence. Unless I hear otherwise by Wednesday, I will report the current version to my director.
... ... ...
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by Wednesday, I will report the current version to my director.
... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.
Here is the one thing to remember today. Before the holiday, get the chief accountant's three answers, and put the sales cost approval document into the groupware.
Everything else can wait until Wednesday, but these two cannot. You did a lot last week. Keep the same pace for one more day, and then enjoy your holiday.
Have a good day, Anthony. See you on Wednesday.
